Executive overview

What the research supports

125 source records and leads across engines, automatics, packages and whole donors. The original 113-record market snapshot is supplemented by 12 separately labelled Kijiji leads; Facebook item-level evidence remains unavailable. Compare the actual assembly, not just the badge.

Finding 01

S55 benchmark

Provisional fair engine-only buying band: US$10,000–12,500 (C$14,136–17,670), conditional on healthy condition and verified dress. Exact matched sample is insufficient.

Finding 02

Value front-runner

Ordinary B58 luxury-car and SUV donors offer substantial asking-price savings. Compare generations and attached hardware before paying for a sportier badge.

Finding 03

Evidence before precision

Bids are not sale prices. Seller “complete” is not a parts inventory. No defensible dressed size or mass comparison against the LNF was established.

Search beyond the obvious donors

The buying workbench

Build a search, check what the seller actually includes, and keep the delivered cost separate from the asking price.

Search engines, packages & part-outs

These are live search shortcuts, not inspected listings or proof of availability. Facebook may require login and uses your selected location/radius; change it inside Marketplace. Kijiji defaults to Canada. Indexed searches can miss fresh or private ads and can retain expired ones.

Search the ordinary donor names too

Repeat with motor, engine, complete engine, dropout, engine transmission, part out, parting out, dismantling, half cut, front clip, salvage. In Québec also try moteur, transmission, pour pièces, accidentée. Search one donor at a time; an engine code alone misses badly titled inventory.

Use the donor map below to check model years before treating a search hit as the right engine. A 740i or M2 badge alone does not identify its engine generation. VIN, production month and the actual engine/gearbox labels decide.

Before calling anything a bargain

1. Identify the actual assembly
  • Donor VIN, production month, original market, engine code/stamp and recycler stock number.
  • Original engine, replacement or rebuild? Exact generation and emissions variant; longitudinal/transverse; RWD/xDrive; conventional, 48 V or plug-in hybrid.
  • Gearbox tag, BMW part number and ZF/Getrag number; bellhousing/case, output flange or transfer-case interface. A shared “8HP” label is insufficient.
2. Define “dressed” in writing
  • Turbo(s), manifold, intake/charge cooler, throttle, fuel rail, injectors and high-pressure pump(s).
  • Oil pan and pickup, oil/coolant pumps and housings, alternator/starter, brackets/pulleys and A/C compressor if offered.
  • For a gearbox: torque converter or DCT clutch assembly, pan, cooler connections, output parts, and transfer case if advertised. Record missing items individually.
  • External radiators/heat exchangers are not automatically included. Package photos must match the parts being sold.
3. Establish condition and mileage
  • Mileage units and evidence: odometer/VIN record, seller statement, or unknown. An odometer documents the car, not automatically a replacement engine.
  • Cold-start/run video before dismantling; compression/leak-down results with conditions and cylinder values; oil/filter inspection and known oil-pressure history.
  • Crash impact location, broken castings/mounts, sump damage, water/fire exposure, storage and open-port protection, turbo damage, prior tune or track use.
  • Gearbox engagement/shift evidence, fluid condition, fault history and known repairs. “Run & Drive” auction language is not a mechanical warranty.
4. Agree the transaction and delivery
  • Written price/currency, seller identity, stock confirmation, warranty/return terms and any race-use exclusions, core charge and refund conditions.
  • Pickup vs freight, crate, commercial/residential destination, liftgate, insurance, border broker and taxes. Obtain an Ontario delivery quote.
  • Whole donor: title/ownership, buyer eligibility, keys, towing/loading, storage deadlines and fees. Keep resale proceeds separate until actually supported.

Ontario delivered-cost worksheet

A purchase worksheet, not a freight or tax quote. Enter every line; use 0 only where confirmed. Blank means unknown. Taxes are an entered amount so this does not silently assume the tax treatment of parts, auctions and whole vehicles is identical.

Reference: Bank of Canada, 24 September 2026; actual payment rate/spread may differ. This does not refresh automatically.

Includes only the lines above. For whole donors also account for towing/storage/disposal. Do not subtract speculative part-out income or a refundable core deposit from the cash needed to acquire the donor.

How this link and Google Drive fit together

A hosted URL can serve the latest published version to anyone with the link. Updates are visible after republishing and reloading; prices do not update themselves. A downloaded HTML is a snapshot. Google Drive can store and share that file, and its Manage versions feature replaces the contents of an existing file. Drive discontinued website hosting, so it is not the interactive website host.

Evidence and method

Research notes

Technical context, sourcing, scope limits and evidence detail. Notes are collapsed and searchable within this page.

The buying decision

Start with a first-generation B58 from a 540i, 740i, X3 M40i or X4 M40i if value matters most. The recycler evidence includes engines with turbos at US$4,700–5,660, before freight and taxes. These share the useful B58 architecture; that does not establish identical sumps, accessories or exact engine suffixes. A cheap luxury-car donor can be more compelling than an enthusiast-car engine with an identical family name.

Keep the S55 benchmark, but do not pay for the M2 badge automatically. An M3/M4 S55 is a genuine alternative; verify the particular output/hardware variant and dress. The intriguing Canadian lead is an unconfirmed S55/M4 engine lead advertised at C$10,000 and 60,000 km by St-Bruno Auto Parts. Its description conflicts with the S55 interchange by saying “3.9”; engine identity, dressing and condition evidence are incomplete, so this is a verification priority rather than a proven bargain. The US$6,500 M2 Competition engine is damaged, not a healthy-engine comparable.

S58 is the expensive step up; B48/B46 is a real four-cylinder path. S58 SUV donors deserve attention, with a US$11,000 X3 M lead against a US$12,622.50 low-mileage M3 assembly. The 2022 SUV crankshaft update matters. Longitudinal B48/B46 engines retain a four-cylinder architecture closer to the LNF; transverse or hybrid variants need distinct assembly comparisons. No defensible dressed-weight or external-size advantage has been quantified.

Original benchmark: dressed 2020 M2 Competition, about 55,000 km

There is no adequately documented healthy, fully dressed exact-year/55,000-km cohort in the captured evidence. Its empirical mean and median are therefore unavailable. “55,000 km” is about 34,175 miles, not 55,000 miles. All listing mileages remain seller-stated unless an auction labels the odometer actual; none was independently verified against service records.

Two adjacent-mileage 2021 M2 Competition recycler assemblies, at 29,000 and 33,000 miles, ask US$12,495 and US$12,500. Their mean and median are US$12,497.50 (C$17,666); dress is unspecified, so this is an assembly-price reference, not a dressed benchmark. A 2020 M2 Competition at 50,285 miles asks US$10,500 with turbos, but is materially higher mileage. A fully described M4 assembly with turbos/accessories at 87,498 miles asks US$10,495; a single item cannot establish a robust market average.

For a healthy engine whose turbos, intake/fuel equipment and necessary engine accessories are actually included, my provisional purchase-screening judgments are (the captured asks do not establish a matched dressed-engine market band):

Purchase judgment USD engine-only CAD equivalent Interpretation
Great Below $10,000 Below $14,136 Worth prioritizing if the 55,000-km claim, health and dress hold up. A damaged or incomplete engine does not qualify just because it is cheap.
Fair $10,000–12,500 $14,136–17,670 Anchored by captured M2 assemblies and M3/M4 turbo-equipped substitutes; this is buyer judgment, not a mileage-regression result.
High Above $12,500 Above $17,670 Needs unusually strong contents/test evidence or another tangible benefit to beat the alternatives.

Confidence is low-to-moderate, because the nearest low-mileage observations have incomplete dressing information and the fully specified observation is much higher mileage. No arbitrary mileage discount is used. A matched DCT package should be compared with the separate engine and exact-transmission asks; no fixed package premium or discount is assumed. The advertised US$14,950 RacingJunk package is stale and inaccessible, and its transmission identity is unresolved; it does not establish a current package market price.

What constitutes the same useful engine?
Candidate Cheaper donors to search Important distinction
S55 F80 M3; F82/F83 M4 including convertibles Same family as M2 Competition, but Competition/CS bedplate, cooling/package and GTS water-injection variants prevent universal tune-only equivalence. GTS water injection is not port fuel injection.
S58 F97 X3 M / F98 X4 M Genuine S58, not B58. Early SUV versus MY2022-on crankshaft matters. BMW's no-hardware-difference statement covers contemporary regular/Competition G80/G82 engines, not every S58 ever built.
B58 original 540i, 740i, 640i GT, X3/X4 M40i as well as 340i/440i/M240i Strong value cohort. Distinguish drivetrain/sump/accessory configuration and exact suffix.
B58 technical updates 840i, newer 540i/740i, X5/X6/X7 40i, M340i/M440i, Z4/Supra Integrated versus separate exhaust-manifold heads, fuel-pressure/cooling revisions and later dual-injection/Miller-cycle hardware are material. “Gen 2” is not a sufficient parts identity.
B58 plug-in hybrid / mild hybrid 745e/750e, Canadian 550e, X5 45e/50e and newer 48 V cars/SUVs Real engine candidates, but electric-machine placement and hybrid-specific transmission/front-end arrangements mean the complete package is different. Power-system output is not combustion-engine output.
B48/B46 longitudinal 230i/330i/430i/530i, X3/X4 30i, Z4 30i, Supra 2.0; 330e/530e/740e separately Useful four-cylinder alternatives; emissions suffix, generation, head, turbo and hybrid configuration matter. Cheaper does not imply the same upper-output internals.
B48 transverse X1/X2, 2-Series Gran Coupe, related MINI Different layout and transmission family. Still interesting for a fabrication-intensive race car, but not a like-for-like longitudinal dropout.
N55 ordinary / special 135i/335i/535i/640i/740i and 35i SUVs; original M2 and X4 M40i separately Original M2 is N55, not S55; BMW specifies M-derived pistons/bearing shells and track-oriented oiling. Ordinary N55 prices cannot appraise an M2 N55.

The detailed manufacturer-source appendices below carry application years, type codes and unresolved boundaries. Badge alone is never accepted as proof of a particular engine generation.

Engines, gearboxes and packages are different markets

The original B58 turbo-equipped recycler cohort has n=4, US$4,700–5,660, mean US$5,177.50 and median US$5,175 (C$7,319 / C$7,315). These are higher-mileage engines with incomplete accessory inventories. The G8x S58 seller-described complete/dropout cohort has n=3, US$12,622.50–13,889.90, mean US$13,337.47 and median US$13,500 (C$18,854 / C$19,084); one has unknown mileage. The early X3 M S58 is a separate n=1 observation at US$11,000. Fully dressed, known-mileage family-wide averages are not established for B48/B46 or N55.

There is no verified current S58 engine-plus-transmission package or B48/N55 package cohort in this sample. Adding separate component asks is useful for comparing alternatives, but is not evidence that a seller will offer that combination for the summed price. Factory S55 cars used DCT when automatic; an S55–8HP combination is an aftermarket pairing. Factory S58 automatics are M 8HP units, not DCT. The gearbox appendix distinguishes 45/50/51/76, transmission-only 70/75 candidates, newer 48 V 60MH-family evidence and PHEV 75/80 families. The newer X5 50e catalogue labels its unit GA8HP80XPH; that is materially different from treating every hybrid as a 330e 8P75H.

The S58 sellers show US$350 freight in their listings, but its destination/eligibility is not an Ontario quotation; it is excluded above. For a whole donor, acquisition cost is hammer/buy-now price plus the actual buyer, bidding, gate, transport, storage, tax and import charges. Conservative part-out proceeds are set to zero for comparisons because no supportable resale inventory, costs or completed sales were established. A hypothetical net-after-part-out value is not a buying budget.

Search coverage and interpretation

The investigation searched US and Canadian listings across recycler inventory, independent dismantlers, eBay, Kijiji, OfferUp, Craigslist, enthusiast/specialist listings, Copart and auction archives. Live Car-Part searches used All Areas and price ordering, exposing repeated broker listings of the same stock. LKQ inventory appeared through the recycler network; direct LKQ access was limited. Marketplace access did not yield a retained verifiable item. IAA fee evidence was accessible, but no sufficiently documented IAA donor was retained. No adequately documented North American half-cut was found. These are coverage limits, not proof that no such opportunities exist.

Listings are deduplicated by exact item URL and identified stock/donor evidence; uncertain cross-list duplicates remain marked. Multiple parts from one donor are separate items, not duplicate engines. A selected, accessible sample is not a census of all North American inventory. A price visible on a listing page is not confirmation that a seller still possesses the item. No sellers were contacted, no inspections occurred, and no purchases or bids were placed.

Healthy/used asking statistics exclude disclosed damage, cores, rebuilt/core-exchange offerings, ended/archived asks, auction bids and search-only leads. Even retained used-condition listings are seller claims, not independently proven healthy engines. Each statistical cohort names completeness and mileage limitations. Unknown-mileage records stay visible and are never normalized to 55,000 km.

To continue efficiently, search both codes and ordinary terms: S55 motor, M4 part out, 740i engine, 540i motor assembly, B58B30M1, B58B30M2, X5 45e engine, X3 M engine, 530i B46, 330e engine, plus the exact gearbox tag. Search recyclers by donor/year and interchange, then compare origin-yard stock IDs. For each shortlisted item, the unanswered purchasing facts are the donor VIN/production date, documented mileage, damage/run-test evidence, exact attached hardware, transmission tag and an Ontario freight quote. These are evidence needed to evaluate the item, not mandatory ECU/TCU/harness purchases.

Evidence & technical appendices
B/N engines: applications and hardware

North-American BMW engine-family map: N55, B58, B46/B48

Research cut: 2026-09-25. Sources below are BMW/Toyota/INEOS manufacturer material or BMW technical-training material. “MY” means U.S./Canadian model year unless explicitly labelled. Application years are bounded by manufacturer announcements where possible; a question mark or stated gap means I did not find a decisive primary source for the terminal year. This is an engine-family and donor-comparability map, not an installation design.

Short take

For a longitudinal, front-engine, rear-drive-based comparison, ordinary 2/3/4/5-Series BMW donors are the closest-layout examples in these families. N55 335i/535i and B58 340i/440i/540i or M240i/M340i make useful longitudinal baseline references; B46/B48 230i/330i/430i/530i are comparable four-cylinder examples. This is an engineering-layout inference, not a price finding or a fitment claim. Exact sump, mount, turbo, charge-cooling, accessory, emissions and transmission configuration remains model/production-date dependent. Transverse X1/X2/2-Series Gran Coupe/MINI B48s, hybridized units, and the off-road Grenadier B58 are materially less like-for-like package comparisons. No dimensional interchange or swap suitability has been established.

INEOS Grenadier/Quartermaster gasoline: current U.S./Canada B58 applications verified; exact first MY unresolved. BMW passenger cars, Z4, X3/4/5/6/7 and Supra are longitudinal inline-six layouts. These year bands are exact where an official annual/model launch source closes both ends; “onward” or stated terminal gaps reflect source limits, not presumed production. PHEV versions integrate the motor into the transmission and have hybrid-specific accessory/control context. INEOS specifies a revised/recalibrated B58 with ZF 8HP51, transfer case and permanent 4WD, so it is a useful engine-family lead but a poor package comparison.
B46/B48, applications evidenced by model year Longitudinal BMW: 230i F22 (MY2017–21); 230i G42 (MY2022 launch, B48B20O1; terminal MY unresolved); 330i F30 and 330i xDrive Sports Wagon F31 (MY2017–18 supported for wagon; no MY2019 primary confirmation found), G20 330i (MY2019 onward; B48B20O2 in MY2025); 330e F30 (MY2016–18), G20 (MY2021 confirmed; terminal MY unresolved) PHEVs; 430i F32/F33/F36 then G22/G23/G26 (MY2017 onward; MY2025 B48B20O2); 530i G30 then G60 (MY2017 onward); 530e G30 (MY2018 and MY2020/21 confirmed; terminal MY unresolved) PHEV; 740e G12 PHEV (MY2017–18 confirmed; terminal year unresolved); Z4 sDrive30i G29 (MY2019–26; production ends 2026). Longitudinal BMW SUVs: X3 30i G01 and X3 30 xDrive G45 (MY2025 B48B20O2); X4 30i G02. Transverse BMW: X1 xDrive28i F48 (MY2016–22) / U11 (MY2023 onward; M35i variant from MY2024); X2 xDrive28i and M35i F39 (MY2018–23), then xDrive28i/M35i U10 from MY2024; 228i xDrive and M235i xDrive Gran Coupe F44 (MY2020–24), then 228 xDrive/M235 xDrive F74 from MY2025. Related Toyota: GR Supra 2.0 A90 (MY2021–24, BMW-derived B48 family; Toyota identifies a BMW-collaboration 2.0 engine but does not print B48 code in its U.S. press release). Related MINI: 2.0L Cooper S/JCW and Countryman derivatives use B46/B48-family transverse engines; complete North-American year/code matrix is not established in this pass. Longitudinal in 2/3/4/5-Series, Z4 and G01/G02 X3/X4; transverse in X1/X2/2-Series Gran Coupe/MINI. X3/X4 are not transverse. B46 is the North-American SULEV-labelled variant in earlier model material; BMW later lists B46D (SULEV) beside B48E/P/R types and uses B48 designations for several MY2025 applications. Do not assume B46/B48 are emissions-only or part-identical: BMW’s TU training guide specifies B46-specific changes and separate high-output B48 hardware.

The application list is “supported applications,” not a claim that every body was offered in every listed year or both countries. In the B58 map, “onward” means a primary source establishes the launch and a later source establishes presence, while the precise terminal year is still open. Evidence gaps: the terminal MY for several BMW B58 bodies, the U.S. terminal MY for the 640i GT and X4 M40i, the complete U.S./Canada MINI matrix, and VIN-by-VIN B46/B48/TU/TU2 splits in border years. BMW’s 2024 model-code reference guide is a helpful chassis/family cross-check, but does not resolve every year or engine subvariant.

Physical differences that matter when comparing bare donors

N55 baseline. BMW’s N55 training material describes an aluminum inline-six using one twin-scroll turbo, an air-gap-insulated 6-into-2 exhaust manifold, centrally located high-precision direct injectors, Valvetronic and Double-VANOS. The common BMW press specifications give 10.2:1 compression; exact suffix/model specifications should govern. It has a map-controlled/variable-flow oil pump, piston-crown oil spray, and a sump/oil-return arrangement intended to keep returning oil away from the crankshaft under lateral acceleration. BMW’s MY2015 U.S. update notice says X5 sDrive35i/xDrive35i production from October 2014 changes from 2,979 to 3,004 cc. The initial MY2015 technical sheet still lists 2,979 cc, but BMW’s MY2016 technical sheet lists the same N55B30M0 in those X5s at 3,004 cc with 84.3 × 89.7 mm bore/stroke; best reading is a verified X5-specific production revision, not a family-wide N55 property. Verify the individual donor’s production date/VIN/parts before assigning this distinction. The special M2 N55B30T0 is another distinct variant: BMW specifies M3/M4-derived pistons and main-bearing shells. Treat it as a comparison point, not proof that all N55s share those internals.

First B58 versus B58TU. The original B58 is a 2,998 cc, 82.0 × 94.6 mm inline-six with 11.0:1 compression in BMW’s MY2016 340i technical material. BMW training describes a heat-treated aluminum, closed-deck crankcase, LDS wire-sprayed cylinder surfaces, deep skirt/reinforcement and map-controlled oil pump. It uses direct injection, Valvetronic, Double-VANOS, a single twin-scroll turbo and indirect charge-air cooling integrated with the intake system. The training material also documents engine-mounted electronics and model-specific external layouts; it does not establish a single transferable accessory-drive package. BMW’s B58TU training manual documents split cooling (separately managed head/crankcase needs), revisions to the fuel system and turbo/exhaust hardware. For B58B30M1/O1 applications it distinguishes cylinder-head-integrated exhaust-manifold versions from non-integrated versions; the exhaust-turbo housing/manifold arrangement is therefore engine-version-specific. B58TU is still direct-injection-only in the BMW material reviewed; “TU” alone does not mean port injection.

B58TU2 / latest B58. BMW calls the 2023 740i engine B58TU2. Its press material identifies Miller-cycle valve timing, revised ports/chambers, electrically controlled VANOS, switchable exhaust-side rocker arms, an exhaust manifold integrated into the head, a 48 V transmission-mounted starter-generator and a dual-injection system. The 2025 X3 M50 uses B58B30M2 and BMW specifically reports a stronger crankshaft drive, revised main bearings/caps, piston oil-cooling-channel supply and dual injection. The same basic engine designation appears on some other 2025 BMWs, but BMW’s public model material does not consistently state the fuel hardware for every one; do not propagate a dual-injection claim by model year alone. The B58 used by the Supra/Grenadier is earlier specification and remains DI-only in their manufacturer technical descriptions.

B46/B48 and TU/TU2. Original North-American B46 is a 2.0 L longitudinal or transverse application depending on chassis; BMW’s X1 and X2 technical sheets identify the SULEV B46, twin-scroll turbo, high-pressure direct injection, Valvetronic and Double-VANOS, with 10.2:1 compression in the cited X1/330i specs. BMW’s B46TU/B48TU training guide says B46TU introduced a revised head, lighter crank, one-piece timing-chain drive, split cooling, electrical heat-management module, 350-bar injection and DME 8. The guide reports up to 1,043 g crankshaft weight reduction on B46TU; the high-output transverse B48A20T1 instead gets a reinforced crank with larger main-bearing diameter, altered-compression piston/rods, larger turbo, higher-flow 350-bar injectors and revised intake/exhaust. These are real donor differences inside the “B48” family.

BMW’s MY2025 press documents identify B48B20O2 in the 330i/430i and X3 30; BMW explicitly states the X3 30’s new dual system adds low-pressure injection to the existing high-pressure direct injection. The 2025 2-Series Gran Coupe release identifies B48A20O2 and dual direct/port injection; the M235 xDrive release also describes dual injection and reinforced M-specific components, but the public material checked does not provide its full engine designation. A shared type code makes dual injection likely for other same-code O2 applications, but where BMW’s own application release does not state it, that extension remains an inference. Pre-O2 BMW sources specify High Precision/direct injection only.

Cooling, oiling, accessories and orientation. BMW training confirms N55 model-specific oil-pan/snorkel adaptation and the B58/B48 TU split-cooling/heat-management changes. BMW’s X3 M50 material confirms revised piston-cooling oil supply on that M2 variant. None of the sources establishes a single swappable sump, accessory drive, head, turbo, wiring or calibration across a family. In particular, transverse B46/B48, hybrid B48/B58, SULEV exhaust treatment and SUV xDrive sump/accessory packaging need exact-model parts evidence before being treated as interchangeable. This research did not audit those part numbers.

Injection claims by exact evidence

  • N55 (all applications reviewed): DI only. BMW technical training says central high-pressure direct injection; BMW N55 marketing/training material describes no port system. No factory dual-injection N55 found.
  • B58B30M0 / early B58: DI only. BMW training and 2016 340i documents specify High Precision Injection/direct injection.
  • B58TU / B58B30M1/O1: DI only in training material checked. BMW identifies up to 350 bar in later engine material; it does not identify supplementary port injectors.
  • B58TU2: dual injection on BMW 740i from MY2023, explicit; B58B30M2 on 2025 X3 M50, explicit. BMW describes added low-pressure intake/port injection alongside high-pressure direct injection. The 2024 X5 xDrive50e release also explicitly states direct-and-port injection; engine code is not stated in that release. B58B30M2 on MY2025 M340i/M440i: unresolved in the U.S. press sheet despite the same B58B30M2 designation; it cites High Precision Injection in the spec block without a clear port-injection statement.
  • B46/B48 before O2: DI only in sources checked. For B46TU/B48TU BMW specifies 350-bar high-pressure injection, with no low-pressure port system described.
  • B48B20O2: dual injection explicitly on 2025 X3 30; B48A20O2: dual injection explicitly on 2025 228 xDrive Gran Coupe. The 2025 330i also has B48B20O2, but its own release does not unambiguously say port injection; carrying X3’s injection fact over is a same-code inference, not separately verified claim. The M235 xDrive has dual injection stated, but exact full variant code is unresolved in the reviewed U.S. release.

BMW’s term “dual injection” here means the retained high-pressure in-cylinder direct system plus an added low-pressure intake-channel/port feed. It does not mean the higher-pressure DI system was replaced.

BMW N55 / application

Toyota describes the 2.0 as a BMW-collaboration twin-scroll/direct-injection four, but does not print the B48 engine code; B48 family attribution is qualified accordingly.

  • 530e model-year 2021: longitudinal B48-family four-cylinder PHEV with transmission-integrated electric drive.

Remaining primary-source gaps

  1. A full BMW/MINI North-American annual engine-code/production-date table (especially B46 vs B48 border cases and complete MINI applications) is not available in the sources gathered here; check exact VIN and emissions label before sourcing a specific used engine.
  2. BMW public information sometimes uses “B58TU2” in prose, sometimes internal type strings such as B58B30M2, and sometimes only “B58.” The mapping among all North-American model/production-month/type-code combinations is incomplete here.
  3. Public BMW releases do not consistently state port injection by exact variant, particularly 2025 B58B30M2 sedans/coupes. Claims above are restricted to explicit applications; other same-code applications remain unresolved or clearly marked as inference.
  4. BMW service parts catalog/ETK cross-check remains necessary for exact block/head, oil-pan and pickup, accessory bracket, turbo, fuel-system and hybrid PHEV parts. No physical dimensions, weights or donor interchangeability claims are made.
M engines and the LNF size/weight boundary

S55 / S58 technical donor notes

Scope: North American production donors and OEM-confirmed engine variants relevant to the Solstice LNF comparison. Model-year starts below are manufacturer-confirmed; I leave uncertain end years open rather than extrapolate production dates.

Family and NA donors OEM-confirmed variants / useful hardware distinctions
S55 — F80 M3, F82/F83 M4: 2015–2018 F80 M3; F82/F83 M4 confirmed from 2015 through MY2020. F80/F82/F83 reference S55B30T0: 2,979 cc, 84.0 × 89.6 mm, 10.2:1 compression, 425 hp / 406 lb-ft in BMW's S55 technical reference. BMW's M3 CS release confirms a 453 hp U.S. CS variant. The M2 CS uses a modified S55 Competition bedplate (below), so S55-family donors are not all the same build. 2015 M3/M4 announcement, 2018 M3 CS, 2020 model-year guide, 2021 G80/G82 launch, BMW ST1404 S55 reference manual
S55 — F87 M2 Competition: U.S./Canada launch as MY2019; U.S. MY2021 update still lists the M2 Competition with no model changes. S55-derived, 405 hp / 406 lb-ft U.S. tune; standard 6-speed manual or optional 7-speed M DCT. BMW specifies motorsport oil supply and the M4 Competition Package cooling system with M2-specific changes. This is a model-adapted S55 package, not simply a common S55 calibration. The U.S. source set establishes 2019–2021 MY; I did not find a separate BMW Canada MY2021 guide. BMW USA launch, BMW Canada launch, BMW U.S. 2020 update, BMW U.S. MY2021 update
S55 — F87 M2 CS: U.S. MY2020; BMW Canada announced the Canadian market launch for April 2020. Same S55B30T0 code, uprated to 444 hp / 406 lb-ft; U.S. car offered 6-speed manual or 7-speed DCT. BMW North America training material says it uses the S55 from the F82/F83 M4 Competition and describes a modified, higher-rigidity S55 Competition bedplate. Preserve this as a real hardware variant; don't generalize all S55 donors as tune-only equivalents. The detailed training PDF is a BMW document mirrored by BMW Repair Guide. BMW USA release, BMW Canada launch notice, BMW NA training manual mirror
S58 — F97 X3 M / F98 X4 M: introduced as 2020 U.S. models. F97 X3 M's final year is inferred as MY2024 because BMW's all-new MY2025 X3 lineup uses X3 M50 rather than X3 M; I did not verify an equivalent F98 X4 M cutoff, so its final donor MY remains unresolved here. Initial base / Competition ratings were 473 / 503 hp. For MY2022 BMW explicitly says X3 M/X4 M adopted the forged lightweight crankshaft used by M3/M4, alongside revised torque ratings. Treat pre- and post-MY2022 SUV engines as different sourcing variants; the engine-family code alone does not establish crankshaft parity. 2020 U.S. launch, 2022 U.S. update, 2025 X3 generation
S58 — G80 M3 / G82 M4: 2021 models; G83 M4 Convertible added for 2022. Initial U.S. base / Competition ratings were 473 / 503 hp. BMW's Feb. 2021 M-engine developer FAQ says regular and Competition S58 engine components have no hardware difference; it is expressly about the contemporary G80/G82 M3/M4 variants, not every S58 application or later special edition. Initial RWD base models paired the 6-speed manual; Competition models paired the automatic (M xDrive Competition arrived summer 2021). 2021 M3/M4 launch, BMW M hardware FAQ, Canada G83 launch
S58 — G87 M2: introduced for 2023; 2025 update raises output; 2026 M2 CS is a Canadian/U.S. donor. 2023 M2: 453 hp, 6-speed manual or 8-speed M Steptronic. MY2025: 473 hp, with torque dependent on transmission (manual 406 lb-ft; automatic 443 lb-ft). 2026 M2 CS: 523 hp, 479 lb-ft, standard 8-speed automatic; BMW attributes its power increase to engine-management changes. These are tune/package differences unless source evidence shows more. 2023 M2, 2025 M2, 2026 M2 CS, U.S., Canada

S55 versus S58: practical hardware differences

BMW's M straight-sixes share 3.0 L inline-six, direct-injection / Valvetronic architecture and twin mono-scroll turbos, but have distinct internals and oil systems. ST1404 describes the S55's aluminum closed-deck crankcase with LDS-coated liners, 84.0 × 89.6 mm bore/stroke, 10.2:1 compression, 3rd-generation Valvetronic, forged-steel crankshaft and 200-bar high-pressure injection. Its motorsport-oriented oiling adds a separate suction pump that returns oil from the turbos and front sump. ST1926 describes the S58 at 84.0 × 90.0 mm, 9.3:1, with a racing-adapted head using a 3D-printed cooling core and 4th-generation Valvetronic; HDE6 reaches 350 bar, the pistons are forged, and a compact spur-gear pump with twin return pumps, a front buffer sump and centrally switchable piston cooling supports high-speed/high-acceleration use. BMW's G80/G82 launch independently identifies a rigid closed-deck S58 block and mono-scroll turbos. ST1926 says the S58 is based on B58TU but that most components are new or synergy parts; this is not evidence of broad B58 interchangeability. The sourced material supports architecture differences, not swap performance or fitment. BMW ST1404 S55, BMW ST1926 S58, BMW 2021 M3/M4 technical release

LNF comparison boundary

The Solstice GXP's LNF is a 1,998 cc inline-four; DOE-hosted ORNL research identifies 86 × 86 mm bore/stroke, 9.2:1 compression and side-mounted direct injection. The BMW figures above are internal geometry only (S55 2,979 cc, 84 × 89.6 mm; S58 2,993 cc, 84 × 90 mm), not engine-envelope measurements. The manuals confirm direct/high-pressure injection for S55/S58; they do not support port-plus-direct injection for these engines. DOE/ORNL LNF study, BMW ST1404 S55 reference manual, BMW ST1926 S58 reference manual mirror

Engine OEM whole-engine mass located Direct OEM external dimensions located Use in comparison
B48/B46 No comparable OEM dressed mass established in this investigation. None with a consistent dressed boundary. Four-cylinder layout is known; no numerical size/weight delta versus LNF is claimed.
B58 No comparable OEM dressed mass established in this investigation. None with a consistent dressed boundary. Unqualified online bare-engine or shipping weights are not substituted for dressed mass.
LNF None with a verified, stated dressed boundary. None. Leave mass and external envelope unknown. DOE/ORNL supplies bore/stroke only.
S55 BMW ST1404 table reports 205 kg / 452 lb for F80/F82 S55B30T0. It does not define included accessories or dressed boundary and is not an M2 Competition-specific value. None. Preserve as a source figure, but do not compare it to the dressed 2020 M2 Competition benchmark or a bare LNF.
S58 ST1926's F97/F98 reference table reports a crankshaft component at approx. 21.2 kg; this is not engine mass. BMW's 2021 M-engine FAQ separately says the contemporary G80/G82 M3/M4 S58 crank is almost 2 kg lighter than the approx. 21 kg S55 crank. The 2022 X3 M/X4 M update identifies adoption of the M3/M4 lightweight crank, but BMW does not reconcile these apparently different crank figures; preserve the application/version conflict. None. No whole-engine mass comparison. Do not turn crank or shipping weights into dressed-engine estimates.

No primary BMW/GM external-envelope dimensions or directly comparable dressed engine masses were found. No shipping-carton dimensions or third-party bare-weight claims are used. Factory vehicle curb weights are not engine weights.

Evidence access notes

  • BMW's canonical Techinfo URLs for ST1404 and ST1926 returned HTTP 404 during retrieval. The manuals were read from mirrors; BMW Techinfo search-index text also exposed the S55 205 kg row and S58 manual contents. Retain this retrieval limitation when citing the exact training-manual facts.
  • The DOE/ORNL source is a government technical project report, not a GM publication; use it only for the listed stock LNF geometry and injection facts.
  • Other BMW North American S58 special editions (M3 CS, M4 CSL/CS, and later model-year power updates) have distinct ratings. Their existence reinforces the variant boundary; this note does not claim their internals are identical to ordinary M3/M4 engines. BMW describes the 2023 M4 CSL as a 543 hp S58 with detail modifications, and the 2024 M3 CS as 40 hp above M3 Competition.
Gearbox variants, factory pairings and prices

BMW DCT and ZF 8HP transmission map

Observed 2026-09-25 for the contract's North American drivetrain scope. This is a documentary fitment map, not an interchange or engineering acceptance. BMW factory designations, ZF family labels, catalog codes, seller descriptions, and swap claims are kept distinct. A named 8HP family is not by itself a guarantee of engine fit, bellhousing match, torque capacity in a particular application, output geometry, controls compatibility, or completeness.

Findings

BMW's longitudinal non-hybrid automatic pairings in the target engine set span 8HP45, 8HP50, 8HP51, and more recent 8HP60MH-family applications; S58 M cars use BMW's M8HP76. BMW's S55-era F-series cars have a factory 7-speed DCT option, not a factory 8HP. BMW DCT code evidence is internally ambiguous at the family-label level: BMW training material discusses GS7D36BG as the structural basis and an S55-adapted bellhousing, while a BMW parts-catalog mirror labels the F80 M3 DCT diagram GS7D36SG; the N55 F87 M2 parts diagram also uses GS7D36SG. Therefore the GS7D36SG text on an advertised unit neither proves nor disproves F80/F82 S55 fitment. The 8P75H / BMW GA8P75HZ in 330e cars is a plug-in-hybrid transmission architecture, not the ordinary converter-based 8HP75. Newer fourth-generation plug-in hybrids use 8P80PH / 8P80XPH families. ZF's catalog contains 8HP70 and 8HP75 families; while not asserted as factory pairings to the named target engines in the reviewed examples, V8/diesel versions are separate transmission-only purchase/adaptation candidates because fabrication is allowed. In particular, BMW F97/F98 X3 M/X4 M S58 is M8HP76, not M8HP75.

These rows are positive examples, not a claim that every year, emissions submodel, chassis, and drive configuration in a model range uses one immutable gearbox. BMW production changes and market-specific parts supersessions matter.

Physical distinctions that matter to a donor search

DCT versus 8HP. GS7D36-series M DCT is a dual-clutch gearbox with two wet clutches and nested input shafts; it is not a torque-converter automatic. BMW F80/F82 training material says the housing and shaft bearing are based on GS7D36BG and that the engine connection (bellhousing) was adapted for S55. Separately, a BMW parts-catalog mirror labels the F80 M3 DCT diagram GS7D36SG, and the N55 F87 M2 DCT diagram is also GS7D36SG. Preserve this source/code conflict: it does not establish that S55 and N55 units share every physical interface, nor that seller use of GS7D36SG makes a F80/F82 donor impossible. A code string by itself is insufficient to accept or reject fit. Obtain the photographed transmission tag, BMW part number, and donor VIN/build record.

RWD versus AWD. BMW parts identifiers commonly use Z for longitudinal RWD variants and X/X-drive for AWD variants, while individual BMW internal codes do not follow one universal text pattern. A RWD transmission normally terminates in its rear propeller-shaft output arrangement. The AWD unit must mate to the vehicle's transfer-case/front-drive takeoff, with corresponding case/output and packaging changes. An AWD gearbox therefore is not simply a RWD box with an extra shaft, and a listing that says “AWD” while omitting the X code is not a verified X unit. The associated transfer case is a separate assembly and is often not included in a used-transmission listing. Never infer interchange from 8HP50/8HP51 family alone.

Converter versus hybrid motor. Conventional ZF 8HP installations use a torque converter/lock-up clutch and model-specific converter, flexplate/drive plate, bellhousing, input, and pump parts. BMW parts diagrams identify converter assemblies for conventional ZF automatics. The 330e GA8P75HZ instead packages an electric machine, separation clutch, and associated torsional damping where the standard automatic has a converter arrangement. BMW G20 PHEV training documentation describes this different layout. A marketplace catalog field that says “torque converter” is not proof that the PHEV unit includes one. ZF 8HP HIS denotes hydraulic impulse storage for stop-start operation; it does not mean hybrid propulsion. ZF's later 8P75H/8P75PH is hybrid nomenclature, distinct from ordinary 8HP75.

Bellhousing and other interfaces. BMW application-specific transmission variants can differ at the engine-side housing/interface, converter/flexplate or hybrid separation assembly, input shaft, mechatronics/software, sump/cooling connections, mounts, output flange, and AWD transfer-case joint. This research found no authoritative universal dimensions or bolt-pattern table sufficient to design a swap. Obtain the exact transmission tag and BMW part number and inspect the mating components; this report does not state dimensions or torque ratings by nominal family number.

Family labels and near-matches

ZF's 2026 reman catalogue lists 8HP45, 8HP50, 8HP51, 8HP70, 8HP75, 8HP76 and additional families, including Z/X, HIS, or hybrid entries where offered. ZF's current TE-ML 11 service list separately names 8HP80, 8HP80MH/XMH, 8P80PH, and 8P80XPH. ZF's older North American 2018 reman catalogue contains older 8HP45/45X, 8HP55A, 8HP70/70X/70HIS, 8HP90 and 8P70H sections. These catalogues establish serviced families; they are not interchange charts or a vehicle/engine approval. With fabrication allowed, V8/diesel transmission-only units can be investigated as adaptation donors, but remain mechanically and electronically unqualified for target engines until specific work verifies them.

The 2015 BMW X5 U.S. technical table is a useful guard against false assignment: N55B30M0 X5 sDrive35i and xDrive35i use 8HP45, while the adjacent N63B44O1 xDrive50i and N57D30O1 xDrive35d use 8HP75. BMW U.S. 2017 5 Series data pairs B46 530i and B58 540i with 8HP50. A 2016 7 Series U.S. technical sheet similarly pairs 740i with 8HP50 and 750i xDrive with 8HP75. A priced 2013–15 750i xDrive listing advertises an 8HP70X. Thus 8HP70/75 donor transmissions are real market candidates for a fabrication-led project, but are not factory pairings to the target engine families on the evidence reviewed. The evidence does not support calling N55 X5 a 70/75 or S58 F97/F98 a 75. Exact VIN/build records could expand these bounded examples.

Fourth-generation PHEV extension

BMW parts-catalog views identify a newer 8P80 PHEV branch distinct from the older GA8P75HZ/8P75H. The G05 LCI X5 50e xDrive (including USA catalog vehicle code 43EU) uses GA8HP80XPH; G60 530e RWD catalog records use GA8P80PH, while 530eX uses GA8HP80XPH; the G60 550eX (including a USA market type code in the catalog) is listed with GA8HP80XPH; and G70 750eX parts-catalog material lists GA8HP80XPH. BMW Canada confirms the 750e xDrive model and an electric motor integrated in the eight-speed transmission. The precise sales availability of each 530e/550e/750e variant differs by national market and production date; catalog records alone do not prove every trim was retailed in both the U.S. and Canada.

ZF's April 2026 TE-ML 11 list names 8P80PH and 8P80XPH separately from conventional/mild-hybrid 8HP80 / 8HP80MH groups. ZF describes Gen4 8HP as modular across combustion, mild-hybrid, and plug-in-hybrid applications. In the PHEV branch, the electric machine is packaged in the transmission, with model-specific power electronics, stator/rotor, oil-pan, mechatronic, and output parts. Do not take the substring “HP80” as evidence that a GA8HP80XPH is a conventional torque-converter 8HP80 or mechanically interchangeable with the 8HP80MH/XMH.

Aftermarket adaptation — separate from factory fitment

Third-party adapter products exist for N5x/S55-to-8HP and related combinations, including Seems Legit Garage's N54/N55/S55-to-8HP adapter and an ADAMAT N52/N53/N54/N55/S55 8HP conversion kit. These are seller claims for aftermarket adaptation, not BMW factory pairings. Product availability or a kit label does not independently establish full BOM compatibility, exact transmission subtype, crank/flywheel/converter engagement, starter arrangement, torque/duty rating, controls, or durability. No independently tested adaptation is claimed here. Fabrication being acceptable under the contract does not change the evidence category.

Sources and access notes

Manufacturer sources are preferred for factory applications and design. Catalog mirrors and seller pages support parts-code or market claims only at their stated evidence tier.

  • ZF Reman Catalogue 2026 (official PDF) — service/reman families including the 8HP45/50/51/70/75/76 and 8P75PH families. The full PDF was downloaded and its text checked locally; this does not make it an interchange guide.
  • ZF Services North America Reman Transmission Catalogue 2018 (official PDF) — older North American family sections, including 8HP45/45X, 8HP55A, 8HP70 variants, 8HP90, 8P70H.
  • BMW USA 2015 X5 technical data (PDF) — direct row-level pairing: N55B30M0 sDrive35i/xDrive35i = 8HP45; N63B44O1 xDrive50i and N57D30O1 xDrive35d = 8HP75.
  • BMW USA 2017 3 Series technical data (PDF) — 330i / B46 and 340i / B58 transmission designations, with 8HP45Z and 8HP50Z entries in the table.
  • BMW USA 2017 5 Series launch specifications — B46 530i and B58 540i models and 8HP50 transmission designation.
  • BMW Canada 2020 3 Series technical data (PDF) — Canadian B48/B46/B58 variant and BMW transmission-code examples, including GA8P75HZ and GA8X51CZ.
  • BMW USA 2021 330e / 330e xDrive specifications — B48B20O1 and GA8P75HZ for both North American PHEV drive layouts.
  • BMW USA 2016 7 Series technical data — 740i 8HP50; 750i xDrive 8HP75.
  • BMW USA 2026 X5 technical/launch material — X5 50e has the electric machine integrated in the eight-speed transmission.
  • RealOEM G05 LCI X5 50eX transmission group — USA-model catalog page lists GA8HP80XPH and related PHEV subsystems.
  • RealOEM G60 530e GA8P80PH parts diagram and 550eX GA8HP80XPH parts diagram — parts-catalog evidence for G60 PHEV variants; market and production details remain VIN dependent.
  • RealOEM G60 part cross-reference — lists GA8P80PH, GA8HP80XPH, and U.S.-coded G60 550eX application.
  • BMW Canada 750e xDrive release and BMW parts-catalog mirror for G70 750eX — Canadian press source for the NA model/motor integration; catalog mirror lists GA8HP80XPH.
  • ZF Gen4 8HP overview and ZF April 2026 TE-ML 11 list — modular combustion/MHEV/PHEV family distinction and separate 8P80PH/XPH group names.
  • BMW G20 PHEV technical training document — BMW training source for the integrated electrical machine, separation clutch and converter-volume difference; live PDF retrieval was not confirmed during this pass.
  • ZF 4th-generation 8-speed hybrid release (official PDF) — ZF explains electric motor integration in the 8P hybrid family.
  • ZF hydraulic impulse storage description — identifies HIS as a hydraulic start-stop accumulator, not a traction motor.
  • BMW USA 2020 X3 M/X4 M release and BMW Canada X3 M/X4 M technical data (PDF) — North American S58 X3M/X4M; technical material identifies M8HP76.
  • BMW F97/F98 complete-vehicle technical training PDF — indexed BMW training text identifies the F97/F98 M automatic as GM8HP76Z, called M8HP76 in the following sections, and notes the transmission converter. Direct PDF retrieval was intermittent during the pass.
  • BMW USA 2022 M3 Competition xDrive/M4 Competition xDrive specifications — lines/spec table identify S58B30T0 and M8HP76; body is AWD.
  • BMW USA 2019 M2 Competition release — S55 and optional seven-speed M DCT in North American M2 Competition.
  • BMW F80/F82 complete-vehicle training PDF — BMW indexed excerpt states the housing/bearing derives from GS7D36BG and the engine bellhousing was adapted for S55. The live URL returned 404 in this pass; recorded as a source-access limitation.
  • BMW catalog mirror: F80 M3 DCT diagram — labels the F80 M3 DCT GS7D36SG and lists BMW gearbox part numbers.
  • BMW catalog mirror: 2016 F87 N55 M2 GS7D36SG — catalog mirror, not a factory technical manual.
  • BMW F87 M2 Competition release — S55 and optional seven-speed M DCT.
  • ZF official current lubricant/service list — includes 8HP60MH/8HP60XMH family labels; not evidence of a specific North American donor's exact code.
  • BMW PressClub USA 2025 3 Series — 48V support and 8-speed transmission at model level; exact 8HP60MH GA code remains VIN/build-sheet dependent here.

Unresolved / preserve for synthesis: exact 2025 North American M340i GA code and transition breakpoints; full VIN-to-gearbox lookup; direct U.S./Canada retail availability of every newer 530e/550e/750e trim; exact physical dimensions and outputs for each suffix; BMW parts-catalog versus F80/F82 training nomenclature for DCT; whether same-seller G80/G82 listing IDs are separate inventory; seller's 8HP75 AWD suffix conflict; discrepancy in the 8HP70 listing price; and tag-level verification of priced units. These gaps are not filled by nominal family labels.

Gaps and caution

The evidence set has one explicit engine-plus-transmission package ask; most sources price engines and gearboxes separately. Transmission labels/codes are retained only where a listing actually states them. The separate engine/transmission asks should not be added to imply a package price. Long blocks, complete assemblies, damaged cores and seller-stated tested engines remain separate categories.

Kijiji search returned Ontario whole-vehicle N55 donor leads, including a 2011 535GT xDrive listing at $6,500 with 186,000 km and a 2018 M2 listing at $49,995, 40,000 km. Direct Kijiji opens returned HTTP 429. These were not engine or transmission part-outs and their snippet prices are not included as drivetrain asks. No seller was contacted. Broader Kijiji part-out coverage remains an access gap.

This file supplies listing evidence only. It does not establish physical compatibility, a generation map, swap fit, seller claim truth, final statistical groups or a recommended drivetrain; mainline owns those conclusions.

Observed 2026-09-25. m_market.json contains 25 individually identified records: current or recently listed U.S. asking-price evidence, ended eBay listings retained as historical asks, one archived S58 part-out, one stale/blocked RacingJunk package lead, and one Kijiji search-result lead whose detail page could not be opened. Search coverage and source evidence

  • Searched and opened U.S. eBay S55 and S58 engine listings, eBay.ca S58 engine and DCT results, and selected direct item pages. Direct pages supplied item price, condition, seller, location, donor/year and mileage for multiple S55 complete engines/long blocks, damaged cores, an S55 DCT, and S58 engine/transmission records. eBay results also surfaced distinct high-mileage long blocks and remanufactured engines; only records with sufficiently specific item evidence are listed.
  • Checked OfferUp and opened the 2020 M2 Competition S55 listing. The seller asks $6,500 for a 30,800-mile engine assembly and says pictured wiring/attached accessories are included. The same description discloses damaged MAF and turbo actuator plus a cracked oil pan, so it is the closest exact-donor lead but not a clean dressed-engine benchmark.
  • Searched Ontario Kijiji and found a result for a Markham S55 motor: $5,999 CAD, 80,000 km, described as removed from an LCI F82 M4. Direct access returned HTTP 429, and the result was crawled five months earlier. It remains an unverified search lead, with no confirmed present availability or package contents.
  • Direct eBay evidence also showed an active 2020–24 X3 M Competition S58T engine ask at $11,000, 51k miles, plus $350 freight. Its compatibility table identifies a 2021 X3 M Competition donor in Florida; accessories and running condition are not established.
  • RacingJunk search evidence describes a complete M2 Competition S55 drivetrain for $14,950 and 56.2k miles, including engine, transmission, DME/FEM/key, harness, cooling and intake/exhaust parts. Opening the source returned HTTP 403; its latest surfaced update is August 2024, so availability and the transmission variant remain unresolved.
  • Opened Project M Motors' S55 rebuild offer, priced at $8,000 plus an unspecified core charge. The seller describes a stock rebuild and a one-year internal-parts warranty. Its warranty conditions exclude racing/off-road use and require an acceptable complete core, which limits relevance to the race-car use case.
  • Checked an archived 2022 G80 M3 part-out. It lists the complete engine at $15,000 and RWD transmission at $4,500, but also says “$13k for everything.” The conflict prevents treating it as a coherent package quote or current inventory.

Best prospects and limits

The OfferUp 2020 M2 Competition is the nearest donor match to the benchmark dressed 2020 M2 Competition S55 at about 55,000 km. Its listing is explicit about mileage and included pictured attachments, but the damaged accessories and cracked oil pan make it unsuitable as a healthy-engine price point. It does not include a transmission.

The RacingJunk package is the most completely described S55 engine-plus-transmission package in this set at $14,950, but its age, inaccessible page and unknown transmission code keep it from current verified stock. It names stock turbos, VRSF intakes, upgraded cooling, oil cooler/catch can, catless downpipes, engine plus transmission, DME/FEM/key and harness. The current eBay X3 M Competition ask adds a US SUV S58 reference at $11,000 for 51k miles, but does not specify dress or engine contents. Among other S55 references, direct U.S. asks include $6,750 for a seller-described complete 107k-mile M4 engine; $8,199.99 for a 92k-mile long block; $8,075 for a 68,228-mile long block with a hole in the valve cover; and $1,699.99 for a 63,130-mile GS7D36SG DCT with cosmetic chips. The $4,500 43k-mile engine has a bad crankshaft and cylinder-5 piston, and the $1,260 long block is explicitly for parts/not working. These are separate condition/completeness classes.

U.S. S58 eBay asks span $12,622.50 for a seller-described complete 2024 M3 engine with 8,102 miles; $13,500 for a 28,586-mile RWD engine identified as S58B30O0; $14,999.99 for a 29k-mile xDrive engine; $13,889.90 for a G87/G8x engine dropout with mileage not exposed; and $17,499.95 for a 6k-mile S58T listing with unclear dressing. A separate 28k-mile G80 Competition RWD automatic transmission is listed at $4,999.01. The records do not establish a current complete S58 engine-and-automatic-transmission package.

Four eBay asks are retained only as ended evidence, the Kijiji lead is snippet-only, RacingJunk direct access was blocked, and the archived G80 part-out has contradictory pricing. The U.S. listing set is richer than the verified Canadian set. No manual gearbox records are included. Neither a shared family label nor seller fitment claims establish physical, electronic, or installation equivalence among M2, M3, M4, xDrive, RWD, or X3 M variants.

An Australian specialist page surfaced during follow-up: its S55 M2 Competition donor engine has a seller-stated 3,500 km, AUD $24,999 ask and listed twin turbos/intercooler, alternator, starter, A/C compressor, water pumps, DME and harness. It is excluded from the US/Canada record set because the seller identifies itself as Australia-based and prices in AUD. A separate eBay X3 M 8k-mile/$13,000 search result was opened and found ended by the seller on 2026-09-25 as no longer available; it is excluded from current inventory and no asking row was added.

The apparent low entry points are provisional auction bids. The $3,600 M2 Competition, $5,200 hybrid X5, and zero-bid 330i/M2 were not completed sale prices; damage, title, fees, transport, storage, and drivetrain condition remain material. The 2021 xDrive45e listing is a useful overlooked luxury-SUV hybrid lead, but the hybrid system and engine were not established as healthy. The 330xe record adds Canadian PHEV auction evidence, though its mileage is explicitly not actual and its sale result was not found.

Separate engine asks put rough advertised benchmarks at $3,500 for a seller-listed B48 with 78k mi, $6,250 for a B58 listed at 65,957 mi, $4,995 plus a $4,000 core deposit for a used S55 long block, $10,500 for a seller-stated 49k-mi S55 in a part-out, and $12,622.50 plus freight for a seller-stated 8,102-mi S58. These are distinct listings with different completeness, shipping, deposits, warranty, and evidence; they are not normalized prices or completed sales. The Craigslist N55 part-out names the engine but does not price it. The separate OfferUp S58 part-out listing is marked sold but leaves the long-block price blank.

Auction fees change the comparison. Copart's U.S. member-fee page lists gate, online-bid and buyer fees in addition to the bid; rates vary by title group, payment method and member pricing. Copart Canada says member fees depend on final price and payment method, with member-specific rates. IAA's 2026 Canadian auction-fee PDF states separate public/dealer and volume schedules; no sufficiently detailed exact IAA donor listing was retained in this sample.

Search limits: no verifiable North American half-cut offer with exact price, mileage and donor identity was found in the bounded search. Craigslist/Kijiji part-out posts often show a generic post price or request contact for a quote; those numbers are not treated as engine or donor prices. Auction “Run and Drive” labels and brief engine-start checks remain yard evidence, not engine-health evidence. No dismantling revenue or part-out profit is inferred.

Live recycler method and deduplication

Car-Part live search evidence

Observed 2026-09-25 in Codex browser, public search form. Searches: 2020 BMW M2 / Engine / All Areas / Price; results S55 interchange, pages 1 and 2 read. 2018 BMW 540i / Engine / AWD gasoline / All Areas / Price; pages 1, 3 and 4 read. Not a complete scrape: selected useful comparable, low-price, Canadian, LKQ and excluded-condition examples retained. Native CAD amounts retained instead of directory USD conversions. Manual-transmission donor engines do not include or target a manual gearbox.

Car-Part combines owning-yard inventory and resellers: same stock/mileage/partGUID across sellers is not an independent engine. AE1450 appeared from USD10,500 to 13,225; B25376 from USD10,495 to 14,774.50. Lowest observed origin-yard ask retained. Large network result counts are not sample sizes. Directory interchange is not proof that every attached accessory or gearbox fits another chassis. Search returned a 2.0L description among 3.0L results; that conflicted row was excluded.

Listing-specific image/part URLs are preserved when present; otherwise seller URL and exact stock number are given. Such links may not display the quoted price; price was read from the search result table. Browser export was unsupported and a direct HTTP attempt returned 403, so selected facts were transcribed from visible DOM. Source search can be repeated at https://www.car-part.com/ . No quote forms, chat, or email submitted. Seller stock availability and engine health not independently confirmed. Grade A is a mileage/age grading rule, NOT proof of successful running or inspection.

The low CP-S11 failed-leak-test S55 is a risk example, not a recommendation: USD3,500 is not automatically exceptionally cheap for an internal-damage engine. CP-B12 USD700 is a block/crank/piston assembly, not a cheap dressed B58. CP-S10 and CP-B04 remain unresolved-condition leads.

The best current-looking engine-only benchmark in the accessible index was the $3,500 N55 from a 2011 335xi; “183K” lacks a stated unit, and its advertised compression test, warranty and video remain seller claims. The $4,500 N55 and $9,000 B58 engine records are old indexed posts, so they should not enter current-price calculations. The S55 part-out discloses serious damage but gives no engine price. Kijiji part-out headers at $1, $777 or $987 are placeholders, not drivetrain asks.

Kijiji surfaced useful whole-car donor asks, including a historical S55/DCT M2 Competition and current-looking B58/S58 vehicles. Keep those separate from removed-engine or gearbox asks. The $800 8HP70 post leaves mileage, testing, torque converter and exact tag unresolved; the existing project notes also treat V8-donor 8HP70 units as adaptation-only candidates pending exact hardware checks.

Facebook Marketplace public searches for S55, B58, M4/DCT and 8HP ads returned a login-gated Marketplace category or unrelated posts. I found no publicly verifiable North American item page there, so no Facebook prices or listing counts are included. The Kijiji and Facebook search templates are recorded in the JSON; several Kijiji cards were rate-limited or old, with their status kept unknown.

I ran 36 query variants across Canada-focused Kijiji searches and public Facebook indexing, exceeding the planned 15–20-query cap. The final sample is still narrow: it did not verify any Kijiji S58/B48/B46 engine-only price, BMW DCT-only sale, or accessible U.S. Facebook listing. No seller messages were sent.

Mainline verification

On 26 September, mainline reopened the GTR Auto item page and confirmed the quote-only supplier description and engine-family claims. The N55 discovery page remained inaccessible and the 8HP search returned HTTP 429; their asks remain unverified index leads. The ambiguous mileage is preserved as 183K (unit unknown), not 183 km or miles. Coverage accounting is two opened item pages, two detailed indexed item pages, and eight card/blocked-item leads. These 12 rows do not change the 21 original price cohorts.
